proposals: Fresh-install credentials use HTTP Basic Authorization; the generic MCP Basic parameters are not interchangeable. Scoped repository denial is not an invalid credential and must not be repaired by increasing permissions.

Docker health and MCP discovery are insufficient new-user acceptance. Check generated credential identity, expected instance UUID, an already-authorized scoped read and separately approved write/readback.

Repeated named-instance installation must preserve data, configuration, credential and organization identity. Keep --instance on management commands and disclose Docker bind-address defaults. New-user tests must not silently adopt or delete existing installations.

Use local public validation and ordinary Git; do not trigger Actions to qualify these fixes. Seven WSL installer cases, three candidate probe paths and a final public-main download/replay with real Agent authoring are historical evidence, not new runtime or cross-version release authority.
